To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TLR-8 agonists reduce levels of airways inflammation and remodeling, and reduce airways hyperreactivity in mice exposed to chronic ETS + chronic OVA allergens.
a Toll-Like Receptor (TLR)-9 agonist inhibits airway inflammation, remodelling and hyperreactivity in mice exposed to chronic Environmental Tobacco Smoke (ETS) and allergen.
a TLR- 9 agonist inhibits airway inflammation, AHR and airway remodeling in a mouse model that mimics human passive ETS exposure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the Toll-like receptor (TLR)-9 pathway in regulating the pathobiology of asthma.
the development of a new class of therapeutic agents that target TLR-9 to treat asthma and COPD.
the role of the Toll-like receptor-4 (TLR-4) in the development of airway inflammation and hyperreactivity in response to chronic exposure to cigarette smoke and allergen in mice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

TLR- 9 agonists can reduce levels of eosinophils and mucus in the airways, peribronchiolar fibrosis, and the thickness of the smooth muscle layer, which is associated with reduced AHR in mice exposed to chronic ETS + allergen.
the TLR- 9 agonist inhibits airway inflammation, remodelling and airway hyperresponsiveness (AHR) in mice exposed to ETS and ovalbumin (OA).
the TLR9 agonist, MGN1703, inhibited airway inflammation and remodelling in mice exposed to both ETS and allergens.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

TLR-7/8 agonists inhibit airway inflammation and AHR induced by ETS and allergens, and that TLR-2 and TLR-9 based therapies inhibit airway remodeling and AHR induced in mice coexposured to ETS and OVA.

we have shown that the combination of TLR9 agonist and ETS exposure is safe in mice and that the combination of the TLR9 agonists and ETS exposure can reduce airway inflammation and airway remodeling in a mouse model of ETS exposure.
TLR9 agonists may be useful as a treatment for asthma patients who are exposed to environmental tobacco smoke.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a TLR-8 based therapeutic could be beneficial for patients with asthma who are also exposed to ETS.
TLR-7/8 and TLR-9 are potential therapeutic targets for treating airway inflammation and airway remodeling in asthma patients who are exposed to environmental tobacco smoke (i.e., passive smoking).
the TLR- 9 agonist, CpG ODN 2395, can reduce levels of airways inflammation, airway hyperreactivty and airway remodeling in a murine model of chronic ETS and allergens exposure.
